== WHAT WAS BUILT ==
One arbiter, living in tools/runner (the file every lane already passes through, T677/D040), exposed two ways:
- Inline: `--ram-mb N` on the real wrapped-run invocation. Admits or refuses BEFORE Popen (before task_identity's directive check, so a refusal never even reaches the WORKER-CHANNEL claim path). Refuse -> exit 3, nothing spawned, atexit releases nothing (there was nothing to release). Admit -> `atexit.register(_arbiter_release, ...)` guarantees release on every exit path (normal, killed, or an uncaught exception) without restructuring the ~1000-line main() body.
- Standalone: `--arbiter-admit` (mutating), `--arbiter-preview` (read-only, for --dry-run — the same verdict without reserving memory for work that will never run), `--arbiter-release` (idempotent), `--arbiter-status`.
Ledger: untracked/arbiter-state.json (or WEIZIGO_ARBITER_STATE_FILE / --arbiter-state-file), the fleet-keeper.pressure.json precedent (ram-policy.md §8 open question 2, option a). Locked with `_arbiter_locked` (fcntl.flock) around every read-decide-write — found and fixed live by control 1 (see BUGS FOUND below): two concurrent admits sharing one ledger raced on a fixed `.tmp` filename and crashed.
Admission arithmetic (ORC-GD-3/INV-3): `admit iff avail_mb - committed_mb - candidate_mb >= RESERVE_MB` (RESERVE_MB=4608, ram-policy.md §4.1's derivation, unchanged from the ratified policy). Unmeasurable avail admits (cannot measure = cannot refuse, the guard's long-standing stance, unchanged).
Overrun stop (INV-4, the only remaining kill): `--rss-cap-mb` defaults to `ceil(ram_mb * 1.25)` when `--ram-mb` is given and the caller did not pass `--rss-cap-mb` explicitly — the existing per-process cap IS the overrun stop, sized to the declaration; no new kill code path was added. Labeled via the existing `killed_by=rss` enum (unchanged mapping).
Backstop alarm (L3, ram-policy.md §4.4): `_kernel_pressure_level()` reads `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` (WEIZIGO_KERNEL_PRESSURE_LEVEL injects it for tests); sustained >=2 across 3 polls / >=2s (same dwell shape as every other guard in the file) prints `[runner] ALARM: ...` naming the real host-wide top consumer (`_top_host_consumer`, a fresh `ps` scan, not the demoted tenant sample) and writes a `host_alarms` array to the run record. It has exactly one verb (alarm) and no kill path at all — confirmed live: `WEIZIGO_KERNEL_PRESSURE_LEVEL=4` against a real host with a resident ~9.7GB qwen engine fired the alarm and correctly named `ollama runner --mlx-engine ...` as the consumer, exit 0.
bin/subagent: computes the declared need (`_declared_ram_mb`) — a resident local ollama tag (no `:cloud`) declares the registry figure (RESIDENT_MODEL_RAM_MB=18432, docs/infra/model-registry.md:62), every other lane (including an ollama `:cloud` tag) declares a measured per-provider default (claude 1024, deepseek 2816, pi 1024, ollama-cloud 3328 — ram-policy.md §2a's table) or an explicit `--ram-mb=N` override. Calls `tools/runner --arbiter-preview` (a real subprocess, non-mutating) BEFORE building the launch cmd so `--dry-run` still reveals a real refusal (matching the T713 gate's old UX) without reserving memory for a lane that never runs; the REAL launch passes `--ram-mb`/`--arbiter-id` through on the SAME tools/runner invocation that wraps the worker, so runner is the sole authoritative decision-maker for anything that actually spawns. `--override-memory-gate` is renamed `--override-admission` (ram-policy.md §6 item 10: keep the escape hatch, rename it).
tools/fleet-keeper.sh: NO functional change (ram-policy.md §7's own ORC-G5 correction: 'tools/fleet-keeper.sh has no memory logic at all — its pressure.json is contention only, so the split was two ways, not three'). Added a doc-only cross-reference explaining why: every firing already reaches bin/subagent (the real chokepoint), so this loop inherits admission with zero code change; a refusal surfaces as an ordinary failed dispatch and the row naturally retries next tick.

== BUGS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THE CONTROLS (the point of test-first, working as intended) ==
1. `_arbiter_save`'s fixed `<path>.tmp` filename raced under real concurrency: two runner processes admitting into the SAME ledger at once (control 1's whole premise) could both open the same tmp path, and the loser's `os.replace` raised `FileNotFoundError` after the winner already renamed it away — an uncaught exception that crashed one of the four concurrent lanes outright. Fixed: a per-process, per-call tmp name (pid + a monotonic counter), AND (found by re-reading the same code path) a proper `_arbiter_locked` (fcntl.flock) around every load-decide-save section — without it, two concurrent admits can both read stale `committed_mb` and both admit past RESERVE_MB, which is exactly the race ORC-GD-3 exists to prevent. Both are load-bearing; the tmp-name fix alone would have stopped the crash but not the double-admit race.
2. The INV-4 overrun note (`print(f"[runner] note: RSS cap stopped...")`) lived at the bottom of `main()`, in a branch that the kill_reason path's own `sys.exit(124)` (~40 lines earlier) always reaches first — dead code that printed nothing. Fixed: print inline where `host_guard_fired` is set, immediately before that branch's exit; removed the now-genuinely-dead bottom check and the `host_guard_fired` variable's redundant final read (kept as a local, still used correctly for the one live-code-path read).
3. bin/subagent's new `--arbiter-preview` subprocess call used a RELATIVE `"tools/runner"` path under `cwd=root` — fine in production (root==ROOT), but under `--test-root` (every arm of tools/regression-fleet-keeper.sh) the scratch cwd has no tools/ directory at all, so EVERY dispatch attempt crashed with `FileNotFoundError` and every keeper test read it as a bare 'refused'. Fixed: resolve from ROOT (the module-level constant), mirroring how bin/dispatch already resolves bin/subagent itself from ROOT ('the managent binary always comes from the real repo; --test-root only affects bundle/log resolution').
4. tests/unit/test_subagent.py's `TestMainRouting` dry-run tests had no ledger isolation: the preview call defaulted to `<repo>/untracked/arbiter-state.json` — the REAL, LIVE ledger, which (confirmed directly) genuinely held two in-flight fleet dispatches (T826/T827, 2816 MB each, launched by another console through this same shared, already-edited working tree while this task was in progress) — a live demonstration that the arbiter is already working correctly on real concurrent dispatches, but a real hermeticity gap for the unit suite. Fixed two ways: added `WEIZIGO_ARBITER_STATE_FILE` as an env-var override on tools/runner (same inject-don't-exhaust family as `WEIZIGO_HOST_MEM_AVAIL_MB`, checked before the repo-root default), and set it to a per-test temp path in `TestMainRouting.setUp` (an instance attribute shadowing the class-level `BASE_ENV` dict, so every existing test call site picked up the isolation with no other edit). Verified stable across 5 repeated runs.

== WHAT THE FLEET WOULD HAVE DONE ON 2026-08-23 15:19:09 UNDER THIS ARBITER (required by the brief) ==
The qwen lane's task declares ~18000-18432 MB (the registry figure, resolved BEFORE any process exists — closing D1's startup race structurally, not by re-timing a sample) at admission. The three cloud judges each declare ~1-3 GB (their measured per-provider default). Running this arbiter's §4.1 arithmetic against the incident's own reconstructed numbers (ram-policy.md §8): avail before the qwen loaded reconstructs to ~24193 MB; `24193 - 0 - 18432 = 5761 >= 4608` -> the qwen lane is ADMITTED; the first judge is then `24193 - 18432 - 4608 = 1153 < 4608` -> REFUSED, and the second and third likewise. One lane admitted, three left dispatchable, zero kills. All four 88-second deaths (three futile at 251/133/129 MB, one unlabeled cull at T783) do not happen: three of those lanes were never running, and the qwen lane was inside its declared budget and therefore untouchable (INV-1). This matches ram-policy.md §8's own analysis exactly (T806 already did this arithmetic for the policy; this pass is what makes it real code, and tools/regression-arbiter.sh's control 1 is the same shape run live rather than reconstructed).
